A docs site built with aiui build ships with a strict Content-Security-Policy and needs no configuration. The policy allows the scripts the site runs and nothing else, so injected markup cannot run a script, and only your own site can show the docs in a frame.

aiui build works the policy out from what the site actually loads: Source Directive The site's own files (app, chunks, fonts, customCss/customJs files, the site.components module and its import map's hash) 'self' The small inline scripts the build writes (theme, URL, redirect stubs) script-src 'sha256-…', one hash each The JSON the build inlines in each page (its Markdown, the navigation and route manifest) nothing: type="application/json" is data the browser never runs Google Fonts and font, stylesheet and script URLs in site.theme.fonts, customCss, customJs style-src, font-src, script-src Integrations (analytics, support chat) each provider's hosts YouTube, Vimeo and Loom embeds on a page frame-src (the privacy-friendly player) The servers of your OpenAPI specs (Try it) connect-src assistant.endpoint, feedback.endpoint on a static host connect-src A navbar primary button of type: github (the star count) connect-src https://api.github.com Everything else stays strict: no 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' for scripts, object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self'. Images and media load from 'self', data:, blob: and any https: host, so Markdown images and badges keep working. Styles allow 'unsafe-inline': the app's code highlighting, diagrams and dialogs set inline styles. The policy goes out three ways: Every built page carries it as , right after . This works on any static host, GitHub Pages included. _headers in the build folder sends it as a header on Netlify and Cloudflare Pages, with frame-ancestors 'self' added (a meta tag cannot carry frame-ancestors). aiui serve and aiui dev send the /* headers of _headers, so the preview behaves like the host. The aiui dev reload script is a file (/__aiui/dev.js), so it runs under the same policy. On another host (nginx, S3 with CloudFront, a CDN), copy the header line from _headers into its configuration.

site.csp Effect unset On for a docs build (reported only when integrations.gtm is set, see below); off for other builds true On, enforced false Off: no meta tag, no _headers report-only Only Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only in _headers and from aiui serve: the browser logs what the policy would block, and blocks nothing a map On, with extra sources per directive (a string or a list). A list with 'none' replaces the directive (frame-ancestors: ["'none'"] forbids every frame). report-only: true in the map reports instead of enforcing. report-uri sets where the browser posts reports Directive names are lower-case words (script-src, connect-src, ...) and sources contain no spaces, ; or ,: anything else is a config error, so the value is always a valid header.

customJs that calls another server (fetch, a WebSocket, a widget): add its origin under connect-src, frame-src or script-src. Raw HTML in a page needs no sources: the page renders YouTube, Vimeo and Loom players, and (all allowed above), shows any other as a link and removes , and similar elements before the policy is ever involved. aiui validate names each one (finding 7019; see raw HTML). Inline event handlers (onclick="…") never run. Tag Manager (integrations.gtm) runs whatever tags the container holds, which the build cannot see, so the default there is report-only. Add the hosts of your tags and set site.csp: true to enforce. Legacy site.plugins: mermaid and syntax-highlight load from their CDN, which the policy allows when they are listed. Other dashboard plugins are not meant for docs pages. To find what a page needs, open the browser console: every blocked load or script is logged with the directive that blocked it. report-only shows the same messages without blocking anything.
